header: Date: 2026-06-29 | Time: 10:00 - 10:45 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (Astra Head of ML), Marco Diaz (Astra Infra), Elena Park (Astra Procurement)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest benchmark runs comparing Redwood to baseline provider (CloudProvX). Redwood reported improved p50 and throughput at comparable cost with some p99 tail variability in heavy concurrent workloads. Action items focused on reproducing p99 spikes, tuning batching/quantization, and scheduling VPC deep-dive and pricing follow-up.
transcript:
00:00 Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh Sofia from Redwood, I think we have full crew, quick roll call?
00:08 Dr. Priya Rao: Priya here, Marco and Elena with me.
00:11 Liam Chen: Liam from Redwood, hey all.
00:14 Sofia Martinez: Cool, agenda is the weekly benchmark review vs CloudProvX baseline, go over numbers, call out anomalies and decide next steps.
00:26 Dr. Priya Rao: Perfect. We're mostly focused on 2 things: inference latency for our triage model and the throughput for batch processing overnight.
00:36 Marco Diaz: Also need to validate VPC and the on-prem-like network egress behavior.
00:41 Sofia Martinez: Great. We'll start with the p0 summary then Liam will walk through the runs.
00:46 Liam Chen: Okay jumping in, I pulled the runs from last night - three main configs: Hosted Redwood standard quantization (int8-ish), Dedicated Redwood with 4xA100 equiv and packing enabled, and baseline CloudProvX standard endpoint.
00:58 Liam Chen: For the triage model with 2k context we saw p50 about 35ms on Redwood hosted, CloudProvX was 48ms, p95 120ms vs 160ms, p99 340ms vs 290ms (so interestingly we were higher on p99 for that bucket).
01:20 Dr. Priya Rao: Wait you said p99 higher on Redwood, can you repeat numbers?
01:24 Liam Chen: Sure p99 Redwood hosted 340ms, CloudProvX p99 290ms, p95 Redwood 120ms, CloudProvX 160ms, so better p95 but worse p99 — likely tail due to occasional KV cache misses and autoscaler spin up in hosted runs.
01:41 Marco Diaz: Were those cold starts or steady-state?
01:45 Liam Chen: Mixed — some runs overlapped with our nightly batch which created concurrency spikes. The dedicated runs reduced p99 significantly to ~210ms with packing on. Throughput for batch throughput (2k context, 8 concurrency) Redwood Dedicated delivered ~420 qps sustained vs CloudProvX ~360 qps.
02:05 Dr. Priya Rao: So Dedicated looks good for throughput but hosted still has some tail in p99. Is that something you can tune?
02:12 Liam Chen: Yes, we have a couple levers: smarter pre-warming, KV prefix cache tuning, and reducing autoscaler cooldowns. Also quantization profile changes — slightly different kernels can reduce jitter.
02:22 Sofia Martinez: Cost note - Redwood hosted run with int8-ish quant saved about 18% unit cost vs baseline for those runs, Dedicated has better unit economics at scale but requires commit. We'll put precise numbers in the spreadsheet.
02:34 Elena Park: For procurement it's critical we see p99 consistently under 300ms for the triage path.
02:40 Liam Chen: Understood. For dedicated config that's achievable; for hosted I'll try changing the routing policy to prefer warm nodes and add a small fixed pool to avoid spin up during peak.
02:51 Marco Diaz: Can you confirm the networking path? When you say pre-warm do you need ping access to our staging VPC?
02:57 Liam Chen: We just need a test agent inside your VPC to generate steady traffic and we can measure warm node behavior. If you can provide a secure tunnel or ephemeral jump host that would help.
03:08 Dr. Priya Rao: We'll share access, Marco will send details this afternoon.
03:13 Sofia Martinez: Cool. Other anomalies - for long context 8k runs, Redwood's p50 advantage grows (we're ~120ms vs CloudProvX 200ms) but p99 again shows variability with large memory churn. That's where packing and kvcache really helps.
03:29 Liam Chen: Right, packing and continuous KV cache reduces redundant token computation. One caveat: heavy packing may increase latency for single-user real-time requests if packing windows are too long.
03:40 Dr. Priya Rao: We have a mix of real-time triage and nightly large batch; can Redwood separate routes and policies?
03:47 Sofia Martinez: Yes route-based policies are supported — you can pin triage to low-latency pool and batch to high-throughput dedicated pool.
03:53 Marco Diaz: Good. About security, we still need SOC2 docs and audit log configuration for Private deployment.
03:59 Sofia Martinez: We're collecting SOC2 and ISO artifacts, I'll share the security pack. Audit logs can be delivered to your S3 or SIEM via log shipping, and we support KMS for key management.
04:10 Elena Park: Great, send the pack to legal@astrahealth.com.
04:15 Sofia Martinez: Will do. Back to benchmarks - Liam, what about p99 root cause analysis?
04:20 Liam Chen: We saw two patterns: one, autoscaler cooldowns causing node churn during concurrency ramps; two, occasional kernel path that falls back to slower matmul path on certain sequence lengths observed in the model, likely due to quantization block size mismatch. We're going to run a targeted trace capturing kernel selection and KV cache hit rates.
04:38 Dr. Priya Rao: How will you share traces? We can't share PII from our infra.
04:43 Liam Chen: We'll sanitize traces and only include anonymized metrics and latency histograms, and we can provide an artifact link.
04:49 Sofia Martinez: Next up, cost/throughput tradeoff — Marco asked earlier about Dedicated commit levels; we drafted an example where a 3-month reserved pool reduced unit cost by ~28% compared to on-demand hosted for high throughput batch. I'll attach that to the spreadsheet.
05:02 Marco Diaz: That number helps. We need an internal cost comparison showing expected monthly spend for our projected 24/7 batch load.
05:09 Sofia Martinez: We'll produce that. Action items captured.
05:12 Elena Park: Any competitive features CloudProvX had that we should be aware of?
05:16 Liam Chen: They had a slightly more aggressive burst autoscaler but no KV cache prefetch, which explains some differences — they get good short-term throughput but higher long-term cost.
05:26 Dr. Priya Rao: Ok final questions — do you support on-prem private deployment? Latency to our internal network matters.
05:33 Sofia Martinez: Yes Private deployment with VPC and on-prem options; we can run a small on-prem pocket if needed, but that's a larger engagement. For now we recommend dedicated pools in nearest region with VPC peering.
05:44 Marco Diaz: Understood.
05:47 Sofia Martinez: Let's recap next steps: send updated benchmark spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 plus concurrency breakdown, provide quantization config and helm values, Marco to share staging access, schedule VPC deep dive.
06:01 Dr. Priya Rao: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
06:05 Sofia Martinez: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and dates.
06:10 End of call

Notes: Transcription includes imperfect match on some product names (e.g., kvcache vs kv cache, CloudProvX baseline). There are a few overlaps and filler words, and speaker labels sometimes generic. Links shared during call: benchmark spreadsheet (link redacted), security pack (link redacted).
